article.title: Cláusulas pequeñas
article.part: Construcciones avanzadas y fenómenos excepcionales — Advanced constructions and exceptional phenomena
article.chapter: Combinaciones avanzadas de cláusulas — Advanced clause combinations

claims.summary: A small clause is a secondary predicative unit with a subject-like element and a predicate but without an overt finite verb or copula, as in I consider [him intelligent] or We found [the room empty]. Adjectival and nominal predicates can occur (They elected her president); the precise constituent analysis varies between theoretical traditions and overlaps pedagogically with descriptions in terms of object complements.

links.notes: Cambridge source supports predicative complements; small-clause analysis is distinguished from a framework-neutral semantic description.
